climate.overview_html: The headline new item on September 10 is Carbon Brief’s September 2026 state-of-the-climate monthly analysis, which confirms the developing Super El Niño is tracking 2026 toward the second-warmest year in the instrumental record — with August 2026 at 1.65°C above pre-industrial marking the first month since November 2025 to individually exceed 1.5°C, and the event itself on pace to rival or surpass the 1997–98 and 2015–16 episodes in magnitude. The WMO SON 2026 Global Seasonal Climate Update (September 8) remains the authoritative anchor: near-100% probability El Niño persists through DJF 2026/27, Niño 3.4 anomaly at 3.6°C for September–November, co-developing positive IOD at ~0.9°C. From the rolling 7-day window: the Copernicus August 2026 bulletin (1.65°C, warmest August and hottest boreal summer on record); the WMO September 3 Super El Niño warning (“off the charts”; ~100% persistence probability through February 2027); the Nepal–Tibet GLOF death toll standing at 1,355+ (1,312 Nepal + 43 Tibet) with ~5,515+ still missing, search operations continuing; and EFFIS European cumulative burnt area at approximately 651,267 hectares, Very Extreme Fire Danger persisting across Iberia, France, Alps, Balkans, Greece, Turkey and Ukraine — now transitioning toward “flash-flood season” as a violent pattern flip brings the Mediterranean severe weather outbreak of September 10–11.

items.headline: WMO September 3 Warning: Super El Niño Could Be “Off the Charts” — Strongest Since Monitoring Began; Near-100% Probability El Niño Persists Through February 2027; 2027 on Track for Warmest Year on Record
items.summary: The World Meteorological Organization issued an unprecedented El Niño warning on September 3, stating the developing event could become the strongest since systematic monitoring began. WMO Secretary-General Celeste Saulo: 'If this trajectory continues, it may be stronger than anything since our monitoring began — literally off the charts.' WMO assigned nearly 100% probability that El Niño will persist through at least February 2027. Climate scientist Daniel Swain estimates ~70% probability this event will exceed the 2015–16 record on the multi-variate ENSO index. Because ocean heat releases into the atmosphere on a lagged timescale, peak atmospheric warming will arrive in 2027, raising the prospect of 2027 becoming the warmest year on record.

items.headline: Copernicus August 2026 Climate Bulletin: Warmest August on Record at 1.65°C Above Pre-Industrial — Beats August 2024 by 0.14°C; Completes Hottest Boreal Summer on Record; 2026 Now ~75% Likely to Be Warmest Year in ERA5; SST Hits 21.1°C on August 22 (New August Day Record)
items.summary: The Copernicus Climate Change Service August 2026 climate bulletin confirms August 2026 as the warmest August in the ERA5 dataset at 1.65°C above the pre-industrial baseline — beating August 2024 (1.51°C) by 0.14°C. August 2026 completes the hottest boreal summer (June–August) on record globally. Climatologist Zeke Hausfather notes that with eight months in the record, 2026 carries approximately 75% probability of becoming the warmest calendar year in ERA5. Daily global sea surface temperature on August 22 reached 21.1°C — a new record for any August day. The developing Super El Niño adds further thermodynamic fuel to the ongoing temperature trajectory.

items.headline: Carbon Brief State of the Climate September 2026: Strong El Niño Puts 2026 on Track for Second-Warmest Year; August 2026 First Month Since November 2025 to Individually Exceed 1.5°C; 2027 Most Likely to Set New All-Time Record
items.summary: Carbon Brief's September 2026 monthly state-of-the-climate analysis synthesises the latest surface temperature, sea surface temperature, and ENSO data to conclude that 2026 is on track to be the second warmest year in the instrumental record — with 2027 the likely candidate for a new all-time record as the Super El Niño's atmospheric warming peak is expected to arrive on a 3–6 month lag. August 2026 at 1.65°C was the first individual month since November 2025 to exceed 1.5°C above pre-industrial, marking a renewed and potentially sustained exceedance rather than a brief spike. The article synthesises forecasts from Copernicus C3S, Berkeley Earth, NOAA, and NASA GISS.

items.headline: Nepal–Tibet Glacier Collapse: TOLL — 1,355+ Dead (1,312 Nepal + 43 Tibet); ~5,515+ Missing (4,996 Nepal + 519 Tibet); Barrier Lake Risk Ongoing; 5,000+ Rescuers Active
items.summary: The confirmed death toll stands at 1,355 as of the latest digest update: 1,312 in Nepal and 43 in Tibet. The missing-persons count stands at approximately 5,515. The disaster originated on August 27 from a glacier collapse on Langtang Lirung at ~5,200 m, generating a seismic signal of Ms 5.2. Debris has been recovered 240 km downstream inside India. An unstable barrier lake at the Nepal-China border remains a secondary catastrophic flood threat. More than 5,000 Nepalese army and police remain on search operations.

items.headline: EU Wildfires 2026: ~651,267 Hectares Burned (EFFIS Through September 10) — Very Extreme Fire Danger Persisting; Rhine Lowest Since 1880; Danube Record Low; Paks Nuclear Curtailed; Europe Now Entering “Flash-Flood Season”
items.summary: JRC EFFIS reports a cumulative EU-wide burnt area of approximately 651,267 hectares, tracking well above the long-term 20-year average of 328,010 ha for the same date period. Very Extreme Fire Danger continues across a broad arc from Iberia and France through the Alps, western Balkans, northern Italy, Greece, Turkey, and Ukraine. Rhine water levels remain at their lowest since 1880; the Danube north of Budapest is at record-low stage; Hungary's Paks Nuclear Power Plant continues curtailing output due to cooling-water temperature exceedances. As of September 10, a violent pattern flip is delivering the first major Mediterranean severe weather outbreak of the season across the Balearic Islands, northern Italy and the Adriatic — forecasters warn Europe is now entering 'flash-flood season' following the blistering summer.

items.source: WMO Global Producing Centres / ECMWF / NCEP / JMA
items.headline: WMO Global Seasonal Climate Update SON 2026: El Niño Deepens to 3.6°C Niño 3.4 Anomaly for September–November; Near-100% Probability Persists Through DJF; Positive IOD Co-Developing at 0.9°C; Both Tropical Atlantic Basins Above Normal
items.summary: WMO's September 8 Global Seasonal Climate Update for the SON 2026 season confirms the El Niño is deepening on its projected trajectory. Multi-model ensemble forecasts place the seasonal average Niño 3.4 SST anomaly at approximately 3.6°C for September–November 2026, with the intensification trajectory peaking in November–December. Near-100% probability is assigned to El Niño persisting through both the SON and DJF 2026/27 seasons. A positive Indian Ocean Dipole (IOD) phase is co-developing, with a SON seasonal mean value of approximately 0.9°C, adding a further global teleconnection amplifier. Both the North and South Tropical Atlantic basins are forecast to remain above normal.

weather.overview_html: The dominant new event on September 10 is a major Mediterranean severe weather outbreak with HIGH RISK issued by European storm forecasters, targeting the Balearic Islands, northern Italy, and the Adriatic coast on September 10–11: extreme instability fuelled by the historically warm Mediterranean Sea (still “charged” from the record summer marine heatwave) combines with strong vertical shear from an incoming cold front to produce widespread large-to-giant hail (6–10 cm), damaging winds, tornadoes, and torrential rainfall locally reaching 150–200 mm over two days — high flash-flood risk from the Ligurian coast to the northern Adriatic and northwestern Balkans. This marks the pattern flip that Euronews forecast in late August: following the record-hot summer, Europe is now entering “flash-flood season.” In the Central Pacific, post-tropical Lowell is tracking NNW away from the Hawaiian Islands after leaving at least 1 dead, ~42,000 without power on Kaua‘i, and hundreds of millions in damage. In South Asia, India’s IMD issued a heavy-to-very-heavy rainfall alert for East India (Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand) for September 8–11, tied to a Well Marked Low-Pressure Area over northeast Madhya Pradesh. SE Asia ASEAN Level 3 haze and Pakistan monsoon flooding remain active.

items.headline: HIGH RISK Issued: Two-Day Severe Weather Outbreak Targets Balearic Islands, Northern Italy, and Adriatic — Giant Hail Up to 10 cm, 150–200 mm Rainfall, Tornadoes, Severe Winds; Pattern Flip Ends Europe’s Record Late-Summer Heat
items.summary: European storm forecasters have issued a HIGH RISK (top-level) severe weather threat for a two-day outbreak centred on September 10–11. Wednesday will see violent severe storms developing first around the Balearic Islands, then spreading across Northern Italy and the Northern Adriatic through Wednesday night. On Thursday, the cold front races southeast across Eastern France, Switzerland, the Alps, Austria, Slovenia, and Croatia. Primary threats are large-to-giant hail (6–10 cm possible), severe damaging convective wind gusts exceeding 90 km/h, flash flooding with 150–200 mm in two days locally, and tornado risk along the Adriatic coast. The Mediterranean's record marine heat content provides exceptional fuel for deep convection. This marks the transition from Europe's prolonged, record-breaking heat dome to 'flash-flood season' — a pattern meteorologists warned about following the historically charged Mediterranean summer.

items.source: Honolulu Civil Beat / CNN / NBC News / Hawaii HIEMA
items.headline: Hurricane Lowell POST-PASSAGE: Weakened to Tropical Storm; At Least 1 Dead; ~42,000 Without Power on Kaua‘i; Poipu Homes Lifted Off Foundations; Waimea Pier Destroyed; First Tornado Watch in Hawaii History Issued; Hundreds of Millions in Damage
items.summary: Lowell weakened to tropical storm status on September 9, turning northwest away from the Hawaiian Islands, but left a trail of significant destruction. On Kauai's south shore, the storm lifted homes off their foundations and split at least one structure in two, carrying part of it across the street. The Sheraton Poipu's oceanfront restaurant was destroyed and cars were moved across the parking lot. North Shore and Westside highways remained impassable due to flooding and debris on Wednesday morning. A homeless man on Oahu died after a tree fell on his tent during the storm. The Kauai Island Utility Cooperative reported nearly all members without power early Tuesday. Hawaii emergency managers declared it the worst hurricane impact on the islands since Iniki in 1992. The NWS briefly issued the first-ever Tornado Watch for the Hawaiian Islands during Lowell's approach.

items.headline: IMD Heavy-to-Very-Heavy Rainfall Alert for East India September 8–11: Well Marked Low-Pressure Area Over Madhya Pradesh; Odisha, Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh in Heavy Rain Risk Zone; Monsoon 2026 Season Toll Passes 100
items.summary: India's Meteorological Department issued a heavy-to-very-heavy rainfall alert for East India on September 8, covering Madhya Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand, and Chhattisgarh for a 3–4 day window, driven by a Well Marked Low-Pressure Area over northeast Madhya Pradesh. India's 2026 monsoon season has now claimed more than 100 lives since July, with Assam hardest hit (87 dead), followed by Kerala (15 dead, 10,000+ in relief camps). Widespread flooding in northeastern India between June and August affected more than 500,000 people and killed at least 99, with research pointing to rapid urbanisation and deforestation as primary amplifiers of disaster impact beyond the climate signal.

items.source: ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre / Channel NewsAsia
items.headline: SE Asia Haze: ASEAN Level 3 Transboundary Haze Alert Remains Active (Since August 26); ~300,000 ha Active Fires Kalimantan; Serian (Sarawak) State of Emergency Continuing; 1.4 Million Malaysian Students in Remote Learning
items.summary: The ASEAN Specialised Meteorological Centre's Level 3 transboundary haze alert, first issued August 26, remains in force as of September 10. Approximately 300,000 hectares of active fires in Indonesian Kalimantan continue generating dense smoke that has pushed PM2.5 concentrations above 500 µg/m³ in parts of Sarawak and Brunei. The emergency declaration in Serian, Sarawak remains active. Malaysia has kept 1.4 million students in remote learning across Sarawak, Sabah, and parts of Peninsular Malaysia. Indonesia's BNPB has deployed 12,000 personnel and water-bombing aircraft across four provinces but dry conditions and El Niño-enhanced drought in Kalimantan are sustaining the fire risk.

renewables.overview_html: Two new deals headline September 10: Google, MN8 Energy, and Eos Energy Enterprises announced a landmark round-the-clock solar-plus-storage project on a reclaimed coal mine in West Virginia, combining 86 MW of solar with 10 MW/100 MWh of Eos’s zinc-based long-duration storage and 70 MW/280 MWh of lithium-ion storage — Google will offtake all energy and capacity under a long-term PPA to supply its PJM-region data centres; and Shell Energy Philippines signed a second 15-year power supply agreement with Greenlight Renewables (a Shell–EPI joint venture) for an additional 120 MWp from Phase 2 of the San Isidro Solar Power Project in Leyte, bringing total committed capacity to 240 MWp. From the prior 7-day window: India’s CEA mandatory co-located storage draft regulation for all new solar/wind above 50 MW, the Qualitas Energy acquisition of Cero Generation’s 5.8 GW European solar pipeline, Heerema’s completion of the Bałtyk 2 and Bałtyk 3 foundation installations in the Polish Baltic, and the Europe autumn 2026 seasonal outlook, which forecasters tie directly to Super El Niño teleconnections.

items.headline: Google, MN8 Energy, and Eos Energy Sign Round-the-Clock PPA: 86 MW Solar + 70 MW/280 MWh Lithium-Ion + 10 MW/100 MWh Zinc Long-Duration Storage on Reclaimed West Virginia Coal Mine; Powers Google’s PJM-Region Data Centres From 2028
items.summary: MN8 Energy, Eos Energy Enterprises, and Google announced on September 2–3 a collaboration to deliver clean, around-the-clock power to the PJM grid from a reclaimed coal mine site in West Virginia. The project pairs 86 MW of utility-scale solar with two complementary storage technologies: 70 MW/280 MWh of conventional lithium-ion storage (operational 2029) and 10 MW/100 MWh of Eos's proprietary Z3™ zinc-based long-duration energy storage (operational 2030). Google will purchase energy, capacity, and clean energy attributes under a long-term PPA and the project will support Google's planned West Virginia data centre. The deal represents one of the few commercial-scale deployments of grid-connected zinc LDES alongside lithium-ion in a US renewable project, and its reclaimed-mine location avoids greenfield permitting complexity.

items.headline: Shell Energy Philippines Signs Second 15-Year PSA With Greenlight Renewables for 120 MWp Phase 2 San Isidro Solar (Leyte) — Total Committed Capacity Now 240 MWp; Phase 2 Online July 2026
items.summary: Shell Energy Philippines signed a second 15-year power supply agreement with Greenlight Renewables, a joint venture between Shell and Emerging Power, Inc. (EPI), for an additional 120 MWp sourced from Phase 2 of the San Isidro Solar Power Project in Leyte. Phase 2 was energised on July 30, 2026. Combined with Phase 1's agreement (signed earlier, energised October 2025), Shell Energy's total committed capacity from the San Isidro project reaches 240 MWp — supplying approximately 100 commercial and industrial customers across the Philippines. The deal strengthens Shell's retail renewables position in one of Asia's fastest-growing power markets and supports the country's target of 35% renewables in the power mix by 2030.

items.source: PV Tech / Economic Times / CEA India
items.headline: India CEA Draft Regulation: Mandatory Co-located Energy Storage for All New Solar and Wind Projects Above 50 MW; Minimum Requirement 10 % of Installed Capacity With 2-Hour Discharge; Comment Period Open
items.summary: India's Central Electricity Authority released a draft regulation in early September that would require all new solar and wind projects above 50 MW to co-locate a minimum of 10% of installed capacity in battery energy storage with at least a 2-hour discharge duration. The proposal targets the growing mismatch between India's rapid utility-scale renewable buildout — on track for ~70 GW of new solar additions in 2026 — and its grid's capacity to absorb variable generation. The rule would apply to new projects from the date of final notification and could affect several hundred GW of the project development pipeline. Industry groups have raised concerns about grid interconnection financing costs and have requested a phased implementation schedule.

items.headline: Qualitas Energy Acquires Cero Generation’s Core European Platform From Macquarie Asset Management — 5.8 GW Solar Pipeline Across Spain, Italy, Poland, Greece, Finland; Cero’s Nordic Operations Retained by Macquarie
items.summary: Madrid-based Qualitas Energy has completed the acquisition of Cero Generation's core European solar development platform from Macquarie Asset Management, gaining a 5.8 GW pipeline across Spain, Italy, Poland, Greece, and Finland. Macquarie is retaining Cero's Nordic operations. Qualitas Energy becomes one of Southern Europe's largest independent solar developers with this transaction, which also includes Cero's project management team. Terms were not disclosed. The deal is among the largest European solar pipeline acquisitions of 2026 and reflects continued institutional capital appetite for early-to-mid stage development platforms in EU markets with strong capacity auction visibility.

items.source: Offshore Wind / Wind Europe / Heerema Marine Contractors
items.headline: Heerema Completes Bałtyk 2 and Bałtyk 3 Offshore Foundation Installation in Polish Baltic — 76 Monopiles Installed; Ørsted / PGNIG Termika 1.2 GW Combined; First Major Polish Offshore Wind Milestone
items.summary: Heerema Marine Contractors has completed the installation of all 76 monopile foundations for the Bałtyk 2 and Bałtyk 3 offshore wind farms in the Polish Baltic Sea — the first major milestone in Poland's offshore wind programme. Bałtyk 2 (600 MW, Ørsted/PGE JV) and Bałtyk 3 (600 MW, Ørsted/PGNIG Termika JV) together represent 1.2 GW of Poland's initial offshore capacity target of 5.9 GW by 2030. The Heerema Thialf vessel completed the monopile campaign in approximately 6 months. Turbine installation and energisation campaigns are expected through 2027.

science.overview_html: Two new papers arrive in the September 10 digest window. arXiv:2609.08241 (EastAsiaClimateExtremes) delivers the first AI-ready benchmark dataset of weekly atmospheric and oceanic extreme labels — anomalously high temperature, heavy rainfall, and marine heatwaves — over East Asia, co-registered with ECMWF S2S hindcasts on a common spatiotemporal grid, filling a critical gap for subseasonal AI prediction research. arXiv:2609.00544 (GenONet) pioneers a Generative Operator Network architecture — embedding a Deep Operator Network as the generator inside a GAN — for stable 3-hour precipitation nowcasting that maintains sharpness and physical consistency at horizons where conventional deep learning forecasts blur. Carried forward from the September 3–8 window: WeatherNext 3 (Google DeepMind, arXiv:2609.03582) setting a new state-of-the-art for probabilistic global medium-range forecasting at 0.1° / hourly resolution by directly ingesting live geostationary satellite data; CloudCast v2 (arXiv:2609.03763) extending cloud-cover ML forecasting from 3 h to 12 h lead time; and the ECMWF AI Weather Quest first-year conclusion with 42 international teams. The period represents one of the most productive weeks in AI weather forecasting research to date.

items.source: arXiv / Fudan University / ECMWF / Chinese Academy of Sciences
items.headline: arXiv 2609.08241 (EastAsiaClimateExtremes): First AI-Ready Weekly Benchmark Dataset for East Asian Atmospheric and Oceanic Extremes — AHT, Heavy Rainfall, Marine Heatwaves; Co-Registered With ECMWF S2S Hindcasts; Open on GitHub
items.summary: EastAsiaClimateExtremes is an open benchmark dataset providing ERA5/OISST reanalysis-based weekly extreme labels and event metrics for three categories — anomalously high temperature (AHT), heavy rainfall (HR), and marine heatwaves (MHW) — over East Asia. The dataset is co-registered with ECMWF S2S hindcast outputs on a common spatial grid and temporal framework, enabling direct, apples-to-apples comparison between reanalysis-derived ground-truth labels and dynamical model sub-seasonal forecasts. Analysis workflows are hosted on GitHub for full reproducibility. The paper addresses a gap identified by multiple AI weather forecasting groups: despite growing interest in AI-based climate extreme prediction, event-based AI-ready datasets for East Asia remain sparse, constraining efforts to benchmark and improve AI models at subseasonal timescales where dynamical models face their largest skill gaps.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.00544 (GenONet): Generative Operator Network for Stable 3-Hour High-Resolution Precipitation Nowcasting — DeepONet as GAN Generator Preserves Sharpness and Physical Consistency at Long Nowcast Horizons
items.meta: Golkar, Alves de Oliveira, Khanjani · arXiv:2609.00544 · September 1, 2026 · cs.LG / physics.ao-ph
items.summary: GenONet introduces a novel architecture that places a Deep Operator Network (DeepONet) inside a Generative Adversarial Network framework as the generator. The DeepONet is designed to learn the continuous-time dynamics of precipitation evolution, which enforces stability over longer forecast horizons and prevents the 'blurring' that afflicts standard convolutional and recurrent nowcasting models beyond ~90 minutes. The GAN discriminator then enforces statistical realism and structural sharpness. Evaluated on high-resolution radar composites, GenONet maintains competitive sharpness and skill scores at 2–3 hour lead times — the horizon where prior deep learning nowcasting systems show the largest skill degradation — without explicitly enforcing conservation laws, instead relying on operator-theoretic continuity constraints.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.04427: Input Data Sensitivity in Deep-Learning Hail Nowcasting — More Training Data Beats Architecture Changes; Dual-Pol Radar and Lightning Improve Skill; Radar Reflectivity Alone Insufficient for Large-Hail Discrimination
items.meta: Pacey, Miralles, Hamann, Martius (Univ. Bern / MeteoSwiss) · arXiv:2609.04427 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: This paper systematically evaluates how input data choices affect deep-learning hail nowcasting skill in a spatiotemporal neural network framework, without changing model architecture. Sensitivity experiments across 8 input configurations reveal that adding dual-polarisation radar variables (ZDR, KDP, ρhv) and lightning stroke-density layers each improve skill more than architectural changes alone. Critically, radar reflectivity alone is insufficient for discriminating large-hail (≥2 cm) from ordinary convective precipitation at short lead times. The study uses a Swiss dataset of 6 hail seasons and evaluates on a spatially separated test domain, demonstrating geographic generalisability.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03582 (WeatherNext 3): Google DeepMind’s Hourly 0.1° Global AI Weather Model Achieves New State-of-the-Art Probabilistic Skill by Ingesting Live Geostationary Satellite Data — Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Maps
items.meta: Google DeepMind & Google Research · arXiv:2609.03582 · September 3, 2026 · Deployed in Google Search, Gemini, Maps, BigQuery, Earth Engine
items.summary: WeatherNext 3 is the first major global AI model to ingest live geostationary satellite data directly and train on raw weather station observations — eliminating the 6-to-7-hour data lag of NWP-based ERA5 initial conditions. It generates new forecasts every hour at 0.1° (~11 km) spatial resolution with an hourly time step, placing its spatio-temporal resolution on par with ECMWF HRES. On both probabilistic (CRPS) and deterministic skill score benchmarks across the full 10-day medium range, WeatherNext 3 establishes a new state-of-the-art for probabilistic global AI weather forecasting. The model is already deployed in production inside Google Search, Gemini, Google Maps, BigQuery, and Earth Engine.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03364: Added Value of Dynamical Downscaling in Sub-Seasonal Tropical Cyclone Forecasting Over the Western North Pacific — GloSea6 Ensemble Experiments Confirm 20–50 km Resolution Threshold for TC Genesis Fidelity
items.meta: Kim et al. (Korea Meteorological Administration) · arXiv:2609.03364 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: This study evaluates tropical cyclone representation in sub-seasonal forecasts using GloSea6, the Korea Meteorological Administration's operational seasonal-to-sub-seasonal forecasting model, over the western North Pacific. Experiments at different horizontal resolutions find a critical threshold near 20–50 km below which TC genesis frequency and track distributions diverge sharply from climatology. Dynamical downscaling of 100 km forecasts to 25 km with a regional model substantially improves TC genesis fidelity, track probability distributions, and intensity statistics at 2–4 week lead times — supporting the case for operational ensemble downscaling as a bridge between global sub-seasonal models and regional TC guidance.

items.headline: ECMWF AI Weather Quest: First Year Concludes — 42 Teams From 30+ Countries; DJF 2025/26 Hindcast Challenge Winner Beats ECMWF S2S Ensemble; Annual Awards September 24
items.meta: ECMWF Science Blog · September 2026 · Competition phase: August 2025–September 2026 · Annual awards: 24 Sep 2026
items.summary: ECMWF's AI Weather Quest — an international competition for AI/ML sub-seasonal forecasting from August 2025 to September 2026 — is concluding its first year, with an annual highlights and awards ceremony scheduled for September 24, 2026. 42 teams from 30+ countries participated, submitting weekly AI-based forecasts for 2-week ensemble temperature and precipitation anomalies globally. The winning DJF 2025/26 hindcast submission outperformed ECMWF's own operational S2S ensemble on the competition's primary skill metric, a significant milestone for AI sub-seasonal weather forecasting. ECMWF plans to expand the Quest to a second year with longer forecast horizons and a new marine heat wave prediction track.

items.headline: arXiv 2609.03763 (CloudCast v2): AI Cloud Cover Forecasting Extended From 1–3 h to 12 h Lead Time at 4-km / 15-Minute Resolution, Trained on Copernicus CERRA Reanalysis — Operational Skill Competitive With Numerical Models to 8 h
items.meta: Nielsen, Bjørk, Dittmer et al. (DTU / DMI) · arXiv:2609.03763 · September 3, 2026
items.summary: CloudCast v2 extends the original CloudCast machine learning nowcasting system — which forecasted cloud cover at 1–3 hour lead times — to 12-hour lead times at 15-minute temporal resolution and 4-km spatial resolution. The model is trained on the Copernicus European Regional Reanalysis (CERRA) and evaluated against HARMONIE-AROME NWP model output. CloudCast v2 achieves skill competitive with numerical weather prediction to approximately 8-hour lead times on continuous cloud fraction, and substantially outperforms NWP at 1–4 hours on rapid cloud evolution metrics. Operational relevance: cloud cover is the primary driver of solar irradiance forecast error at sub-day timescales, making 12-hour ML cloud forecasting a direct input to solar energy dispatch and grid balancing systems.

items.title: Verisk Releases 2026 Cat Risk Report: Global Insured Average Annual Catastrophe Loss Now $171 Billion — Up $19 Billion Year-on-Year; U.S. Accounts for 68%; Severe Thunderstorm Overtakes Hurricane as Top Peril; Record High Even Without U.S. Hurricane Landfall in 2025
items.body_html: Verisk’s annual Extreme Event Solutions Cat Risk Report, released September 1–3, places the global insurance industry’s modelled average annual loss (AAL) from catastrophes at $171 billion for 2026 — the highest estimate Verisk has ever reported, up $19 billion from the prior year. Of the $171 billion global figure, $117 billion (68%) is attributed to the United States. Severe thunderstorm (40% share) has overtaken tropical cyclone (27%) as the single largest modelled peril — a structural shift driven by rapid property value inflation in tornado-prone corridors and improved convective storm modelling. Notably, the AAL rose even after a year with no U.S. hurricane landfalls for the first time in a decade, demonstrating that the benchmark’s upward trajectory is driven by exposure growth and climate-adjusted hazard frequencies, not a single outsized event year. Reinsurers and primary carriers cite the report as benchmark input for 2027 pricing and capital allocation cycles.

items.title: Light (PoweredbyLight) Raises $46 Million Series A Led by Matrix Partners to Scale “Embedded Electricity” Platform — Enables Any Company to Offer Branded Retail Electricity With Built-In VPP Participation; Covers 30% of U.S. Residential Solar Sales
items.body_html: Light (brand: PoweredbyLight), an Austin-based platform that lets any company become a regulated retail electricity provider via API — including licensing, wholesale procurement, billing, customer support, and virtual power plant (VPP) participation — closed a $46 million Series A round on September 1–4, led by Matrix Partners with participation from Activate Capital, Spark Capital, Mischief, Gigascale Capital, MCJ, and BoxGroup. Total funding now exceeds $60 million; Light’s capital base (equity + credit facility) exceeds $100 million. The company’s partner network already covers more than 30% of all U.S. residential solar sales (including Palmetto, GoodLeap, Emporia, Lunar Energy), 500,000+ homeowners, and 1 million+ multi-family units. Run-rate revenue increased 10× over the prior 12 months. In H1 2026, 100% of new electricity brands entering the Texas ERCOT market launched on Light’s platform. Light has joined the PJM wholesale market (13 states + DC) and is preparing expansion into New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Illinois. The funding round is notable for positioning distributed solar and storage assets as addressable VPP capacity within a mainstream B2B SaaS model.

items.title: Swiss Re: Data Centers and AI Workloads Create $200 Billion Premium Opportunity for Insurers — Hyperscaler Power Demand Expected to Triple by 2030; New Nat-Cat Exposure at Scale; Cyber-Physical Risk Convergence Identified as Major Coverage Gap
items.body_html: Swiss Re Institute’s September 2026 sigma report quantifies data centres and AI compute infrastructure as a $200 billion cumulative premium opportunity for the global (re)insurance industry through 2030, driven by the explosive growth in hyperscaler and co-location capacity. The report projects that hyperscaler power demand will triple by 2030, creating new concentrations of physical risk exposure — fire, flood, power-interruption, and cooling failure — at a scale that substantially exceeds existing commercial insurance penetration. Swiss Re identifies cyber-physical risk convergence as the major emerging coverage gap: as AI workloads become operationally critical, a single data centre outage can trigger simultaneous property damage, business interruption, and downstream liability claims across multiple policyholders simultaneously. Nat-cat exposure is also flagged: many hyperscaler campuses being built in historically low-risk corridors (e.g. Iowa, Virginia, Texas) are now in locations with rapidly changing flood, heat, and severe-thunderstorm risk profiles. Swiss Re recommends parametric trigger structures and real-time physical risk monitoring as components of a new data-centre risk transfer framework.
items.source_html: Swiss Re Institute / Reuters

items.title: Howden Re Launches International Alternative Solutions Practice — Dedicated Parametric, ILS, and Climate-Risk Transfer Team; Hire of 12-Person Ex-Aon Reinsurance Team; Focus on Sovereign Nat-Cat, Food Security, and Transition Risk
items.body_html: Howden Re announced the formal launch of its International Alternative Solutions Practice on September 6, a dedicated team focused on parametric reinsurance, Insurance-Linked Securities (ILS), and bespoke climate-risk transfer structures. The practice is anchored by a 12-person team predominantly hired from Aon’s reinsurance solutions division. Priority markets include sovereign parametric nat-cat covers for Small Island Developing States and lower-middle-income countries (a segment historically served by the World Bank’s IBRD and the African Risk Capacity), multi-year food security triggers linked to ENSO indices, and transition-risk liability covers for energy companies managing coal asset retirement. The launch reflects continued growth in demand for ILS-style risk transfer as traditional reinsurance capacity tightens on climate-exposed lines.

items.title: Nexeon (UK) Closes £100 Million Series D for Silicon Anode Battery Materials — National Wealth Fund and Honda Xcelerator Lead; Expands Teesside Pilot Facility Targeting 10,000-Cycle EV Battery Cathode Longevity
items.body_html: Abingdon-based Nexeon closed a £100 million Series D round on September 6, led by the UK’s National Wealth Fund (through UKIB) and Honda Xcelerator Ventures, with Korea Development Bank as strategic co-investor. Nexeon’s silicon anode technology replaces or supplements graphite in EV battery anodes, increasing energy density by up to 20% and targeting cycle lives exceeding 10,000 full charge-discharge cycles — a figure critical for next-generation battery-electric commercial vehicles and long-duration residential storage. Funds will expand Nexeon’s Teesside pilot facility and accelerate scale-up toward a gigawatt-hour-scale manufacturing line. Honda’s participation follows a multi-year joint development agreement. The National Wealth Fund’s involvement reflects the UK government’s priority on domestic advanced battery materials supply chain as a strategic industrial policy objective.

items.title: Qualitas Energy Acquires Cero Generation’s 5.8 GW European Solar & Development Platform From Macquarie — Expands to Spain, Italy, Poland, Greece, Finland; Macquarie Retains Nordic Operations
items.body_html: Madrid-based Qualitas Energy completed the acquisition of Cero Generation’s core European solar development platform from Macquarie Asset Management on September 7, gaining a 5.8 GW development pipeline spanning Spain, Italy, Poland, Greece, and Finland. Macquarie is retaining Cero’s Nordic operations. Qualitas becomes one of Southern Europe’s largest independent solar developers; the deal includes Cero’s experienced project management and development team alongside the pipeline. Terms were not disclosed. The transaction reflects continued appetite from Southern European independent power producers for development-stage pipeline acquisitions ahead of the European Commission’s accelerated permitting regime and capacity auctions under REPowerEU.

items.title: ARC Ride (Kenya) Closes $33.3 Million Series A to Scale Battery-Swapping Electric Motorcycle Network Across Sub-Saharan Africa — IFC, BII, Proparco, Novastar Ventures Lead; 5,000 New E-Motos; Expanding to Ghana, South Africa, Tanzania, Uganda
items.body_html: Kenyan electric mobility startup ARC Ride closed a $33.3 million financing round on September 8, comprising a $23 million Series A equity round co-led by Novastar Ventures and Norrsken22 alongside a $10 million debt tranche. Strategic investors include the International Finance Corporation (IFC), British International Investment (BII), Proparco, Musashi Seimitsu, and Talanton. ARC Ride operates a Battery-as-a-Service model in which riders exchange depleted batteries at swap stations rather than owning them, reducing the upfront cost barrier to switching from petrol-powered motorcycles. The company plans to add 5,000 electric motorcycles to its fleet and expand its battery-swapping network from Kenya into Ghana, South Africa, Tanzania, and Uganda. Africa’s two- and three-wheeler market is one of the highest-emission transportation segments per passenger-kilometer, and battery swapping addresses the range anxiety and grid-charging infrastructure gaps that have constrained EV adoption across the continent.
